name: The Jew's House

dates.altered: C18 and C19 alterations: two C18 brick gable stacks, an early-C19 wooden shopfront in an altered opening, a C19 half-glazed door with overlight, C18 glazing-bar sashes set into the C12 windows, and a segment-headed dormer with a C20 casement.
dates.note: The entry's 'c1170' and the node's exemplar year of 1170 agree.

quotes.text: House, originally with a first floor hall and shops below, now a restaurant and salon. c1170, with C18 and C19 alterations. Dressed stone and brick, with pantile roof and two C18 brick gable stacks.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, opening paragraph following the legacy headers

quotes.text: EXTERIOR: moulded sill band and enriched impost band to first floor. 2 storeys plus attics, 3 bays. Off-centre doorway, C12, with interlace ornament and stiff-leaf capitals to missing shafts. Above it, a shallow chimney breast to the hall.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: Above, two altered C12 2-light windows with heavily moulded heads, that to left with the remains of shafts. Each now has a C18 glazing bar sash. In the centre, a similar sash. Above again, to right, a segment headed dormer with a C20 casement.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph, first-floor description

quotes.text: INTERIOR has in the rear wall a C12 chamfered doorway with imposts. In the north wall, a restored chamfered segment headed recess on each floor.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, INTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: This building is an exceptionally important example of C12 domestic architecture: Lincolnshire has most of the surviving
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, closing paragraph; THE EXTRACT'S SPAN ENDS MID-SENTENCE at 'surviving' and the sentence is quoted only as far as it was read

note: Tranche 3, English medieval fabric and the Tudor house, 5 Sep 2026. Extracted twice with different queries; the first returned only map boilerplate and the second the whole Details section, which is the behaviour WP-11.5 records for these entries. THE ENTRY CORROBORATES THE NODE'S SHARPEST CLAIM ABOUT THIS BUILDING -- that the ground-floor doorway carries the chimney of the hall above -- in the register's own words: 'Off-centre doorway, C12 ... Above it, a shallow chimney breast to the hall.' It states the plan type ('originally with a first floor hall and shops below') and no dimension.
